stem: If $A({=ax}, {=ay})$, $B({=bx}, {=by})$ and $C({=cx}, {=cy})$, find the equation of the straight line passing through the vertex $A$ and bisecting $\overline{BC}$. Write it in the form $y = mx + b$.
solution: The slope of the line through $A({=ax}, {=ay})$ and $({=mx}, {=my})$ is $\frac{{=my} - ({=ay})}{{=mx} - ({=ax})} = \frac{{=my - ay}}{{=dx}} = {=m}$.
So the equation has the form $y = {=m}x + b$.
The point $A({=ax}, {=ay})$ lies on the line: ${=ay} = {=m} \times ({=ax}) + b$.
The equation of the line is $y = {=m}x {=sg} {=abs(b)}$.
notes: Midpoint is built to have integer coordinates and the slope from A to it is the integer m. Follows book example 4, with the answer in y = mx + b form.
